channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Wearable-based digital metrics reveal dynamic dissociations between upper limb capacity and real-world use over the first six months after stroke
item.description: In 72 stroke patients over six months, wearable-based digital metrics revealed that upper limb activity capacity and real-world performance were correlated (Spearman's ρs = 0.45–0.78, p < 0.001) but their coupling weakened over time, with 52% of those improving on ARAT not improving their use ratio, indicating a dynamic dissociation.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Exercise-based rehabilitation interventions for kinesiophobia after total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: Exercise-based rehabilitation significantly reduced kinesiophobia (SMD = -1.22, 95% CI [-1.72, -0.72]) and improved knee function (SMD = 1.19, 95% CI [0.67, 1.71]) in 1,096 patients after total knee arthroplasty, although certainty of evidence was low and heterogeneity was high.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Effects of Neurostimulation- and Technology-Augmented Robot-Assisted Training on Upper-Limb Motor Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 103 trials (5,251 participants) found rTMS plus robot-assisted training (RAT) yielded the largest Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) estimate (MD 9.56, 95% CI 7.18-11.93 vs. usual care), followed by LFES plus RAT (MD 7.52), outperforming RAT alone (MD 3.83).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of Incorporating Perceptual Learning Into Plantar Hardness Discrimination on the Risk of Falling and Muscle Torque in Patients With Hemiplegia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=34 stroke patients) found that incorporating perceptual learning with plantar hardness discrimination into rehabilitation significantly lowered fall risk (P <0.001, ES=1.48), increased knee extensors torque (P <0.001, ES=1.19), and improved FIM scores (P <0.001, ES=1.56) in hemiplegic patients compared to controls.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of different physical therapies for axillary web syndrome after breast cancer surgery: A network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (1007 patients) found that soft tissue manual therapy + therapeutic exercise + low-level laser therapy significantly reduced pain (SMD = -4.40) and improved shoulder ROM, while manual lymphatic drainage + therapeutic exercise significantly improved upper-limb disability (MD = -19.01) in patients with axillary web syndrome after breast cancer surgery.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Altered Cognitive Control and Cortical Oscillatory Dynamics in Athletes With ACL Reconstruction During Decision-Making Under Uncertainty.
item.description: In 90 open-skill athletes (45 non-ACLR, 45 ACLR), ACLR athletes showed slower response times and lower accuracy (d = 0.75-1.09) during a probabilistic go/no-go task, with attenuated midfrontal theta power prestimulus and elevated power during the target phase, reflecting a shift to reactive cognitive control, impaired motor cortical disinhibition, and less efficient visual-attentional resource deployment.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
item.description: An ICCUS Society modified Delphi consensus (n=17 experts) for athletic hamstring injuries (AHSI) achieved consensus on 54 statements (mean agreement 89.88%), supporting standardized terminology, MRI/ultrasound for diagnosis, individualized and criterion-based rehabilitation, progressive tissue loading, early neuromuscular control, gradual running/agility progression, pain-free sprinting, objective strength assessment, sport-specific workloads, and athlete readiness as key RTS criteria.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative study of therapeutic ultrasound and whole-body vibration as adjuncts to passive stretching on knee joint range of motion and functional ability in children with hemiplegic cerebral palsy: a randomized trial
item.description: A randomized trial (n=60 children aged 4-6 years with hemiplegic cerebral palsy) compared therapeutic ultrasound (US) and whole-body vibration (WBV) as adjuncts to passive stretching. The WBV group showed significantly greater improvements in active knee extension ROM (13.82% vs 7.05%) and GMFM scores (22.72% vs 11.32%) over 12 weeks (p<0.01).
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
item.description: An international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomized controlled trial (PROSpect) found no evidence to support prone positioning or high-frequency oscillatory ventilation as first-line strategies to improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome.
item.author: The Lancet

item.title: Adding blood flow restriction to low-load resistance training for sarcopenia and cognitive function in oldest-old adults: an exploratory randomized controlled trial
item.description: An exploratory RCT (N=36) in oldest-old adults with sarcopenia and MCI found supervised low-load BFR-RT to be well-attended and safe, showing favorable changes in handgrip strength, 4-m walk time, verbal learning, and delayed recall compared to no exercise, but limited additional benefits over matched low-load RT.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Effects of chair-based exercise training on pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and quality of life in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD: A randomised controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial of 30 AECOPD patients found chair-based exercise training significantly improved functional exercise capacity (6MWT distance: mean change 79.7m vs 28.8m, p=0.042), dyspnoea, and quality of life compared to breathing exercises alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of 12-week massage on pain, muscle co-contraction, and knee loading in medial knee osteoarthritis: a randomized clinical trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=56) found that 12 weeks of massage therapy significantly improved WOMAC pain, stiffness, and physical function, and reduced medial muscle co-contraction during early stance in individuals with medial knee osteoarthritis, compared to a healthcare education group.
item.author: Aging Clin Exp Res

item.title: Neurocognitive Factors in ACL Injury: The Missing Piece in Rehabilitation and Prevention? A Scoping Review.
item.description: A scoping review of 42 studies identified dual-task interference and visual attention as the most investigated neurocognitive domains in ACL injury. Neurocognitive training interventions show potential benefits in visuomotor efficiency, movement compliance, and return to sport readiness, suggesting neurocognitive factors are a missing component in current ACL rehabilitation and prevention frameworks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of a Structured Post-Platelet Rich Plasma Rehabilitation Approach on Pain and Function in Subacromial Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial of 54 SAPS patients found that adding a structured post-PRP rehabilitation approach to conventional physiotherapy significantly improved pain (VAS: 2.92 ± 1.14 vs 7.96 ± 0.75; SF-MPQ: 10.07 ± 3.33 vs 19.37 ± 2.35, p < 0.001) and shoulder function compared to conventional physiotherapy alone over 21 days.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: First-Hand Experience and the Value of Telerehabilitation for Chronic Knee Pain: A Discrete Choice Experiment Nested in a Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A discrete choice experiment nested in an RCT with 319 Australian adults with chronic knee pain found that participants with first-hand telerehabilitation experience were willing to pay AU$87.49 more for telerehabilitation consultations than those who experienced in-person care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Does low back pain improve following supervised patient education and exercise therapy targeting hip osteoarthritis symptoms? A longitudinal cohort study of 5014 patients.
item.description: A longitudinal cohort study of 5014 hip OA patients found that participation in a supervised education and exercise program for hip OA was associated with significant reductions in LBP intensity at 3 months (19% improvement) and 12 months (21% improvement), particularly among hip OA responders.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Next-generation control strategies for lower-extremity exoskeletons: State-of-the-art, limitations, and future directions.
item.description: This review summarizes current and emerging control strategies for lower-extremity exoskeletons in gait rehabilitation, highlighting their limitations (e.g., unintuitive interfaces, poor adaptation to varying conditions) and exploring advances in user intent detection, such as brain-computer interfaces and novel biosignals.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Clinical approach to balance intensity in people with multiple sclerosis: clinical judgment versus the Balance Intensity Tool for Exercise - an inter-rater agreement and reliability study.
item.description: This inter-rater agreement and reliability study of 61 MS patients found that the Balance Intensity Tool for Exercise (BITE) demonstrated excellent inter-rater reliability (ICC > 0.9) and narrower limits of agreement (up to ±20%) compared to clinical judgment (up to ±36%) for assessing balance exercise intensity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Preoperative factors associated with quadriceps strength 1 year after total knee arthroplasty: a prospective longitudinal study.
item.description: A longitudinal study of 39 TKA patients found that higher preoperative normalized quadriceps strength (B=0.72, 95% CI: 0.40 to 1.0, p < 0.001) and lower preoperative limb symmetry index (B=-0.19, 95% CI: -0.32 to -0.059, p = 0.006) were significantly associated with better quadriceps strength and strength gains 1 year post-TKA.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Low-frequency deep brain stimulation promotes long-term orofacial motor recovery after traumatic brain injury: A case study
item.description: A case study showed that low-frequency continuous deep brain stimulation (55 Hz) of the motor thalamus in a patient with severe diffuse axonal injury and chronic dysarthria/dysphagia led to progressive recovery of facial symmetry, resolution of laryngeal penetration, and marked improvements in respiratory/phonatory control and speech intelligibility over 3 years.
item.author: medRxiv
